deadline_pattern: No fixed deadline: proposals are considered on an ongoing basis and must be received at least two weeks before the event; funds must be spent by December 31 of the fiscal year with no carryover

notes: Washougal runs a rolling Hotel/Motel Tax Application (one form per event or project) reviewed by its Lodging Tax Committee as long as the request fits the adopted budget; the City makes the final call. Committee weighs projected room nights, reliability of the information, promotion of Washougal beyond its borders and spending in the city, and gives priority to broad tourism promotion and large overnight-generating sporting, cultural and leisure events over small single-day events. Awards are reimbursement-only after hard-copy proof of advertising and a post-event room-night evaluation; recipients must credit city hotel/motel funds in advertising. Annual pool and award caps are not published.

name: Ferndale
tax_rate: Rate not confirmed (Whatcom County rows were missing from the DOR flyer retrieved); 2024 DOR distributions $59,249 ($29,625 state-shared + $29,625 special), consistent with a 2% special tax
deadline_pattern: Application window runs roughly June 20 to July 31 (June 22 to Aug 1 in 2022; June 20 to July 31 per FY2026 instructions); LTAC reviews in August and City Council approves awards in early September (Sept 2026 for FY2027). FY2027 window is closed; city says check back June 2027 for the next cycle.
typical_open: Late June (city posts the application in June; next expected June 2027)
annual_pool: FY2027 (approved Sept 2026): $50,000 awarded to 8 of 10 applicants out of $89,500 requested. Prior round: $81,000 to 10 organizations out of 14 requests totaling $171,350.
contact: Michelle Williams, Deputy City Clerk, michellewilliams@cityofferndale.org, 360-384-4302 (City Hall) / 360-685-2358 (Deputy City Clerk line in instructions), City of Ferndale, PO Box 936 / 2095 Main Street, Ferndale, WA 98248
notes: Small annual program run by the Deputy City Clerk: applications are taken in a June 20 to July 31 window, the LTAC scores them on economic impact (visits, overnight stays, off-peak, first-time events), matching resources, fit with community assets and objectives, and compliance with the lodging tax statute, and the council adopts awards in September. The committee can consider off-cycle requests but approval is less likely. Grants are reimbursement-only with 20% withheld until a final written report (documenting tourists and overnight stays) and an oral report to City Council are delivered. Recent awards skew to the Chamber visitor center ($30,000) and city Pioneer Village ($10,000), with events getting $500 to $3,000; Whatcom Frightmare and Rock the Block were declined for FY2027.

pool_note: FY2027 round (council approval Sept 2026): $50,000 awarded; $10,000 went to the City of Ferndale itself (Pioneer Village tour guides), leaving $40,000 to outside applicants, of which $30,000 went to the Chamber visitor center and $10,000 was split among six event grants ($500-$3,000). Prior round was larger ($81,000 to 10 organizations). Total lodging tax revenue was about $59,000 in 2024 per DOR.

tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (total lodging tax rate 10.4%) per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions $34,402 ($16,953 state-shared + $17,448 special)
deadline_pattern: Written Hotel/Motel Tax applications are submitted to City Hall in the fall and reviewed at the council's November budget workshop (Nov 12, 2024 for 2025 funds), with final approval at the mid-November regular meeting and adoption in the annual budget. The 2027-cycle review (expected November 2026) is imminent; no published deadline.
typical_open: September-October (no formal call; applicants submit written requests to the City Clerk ahead of the November budget workshop)
annual_pool: 2025: $50,925 approved across 8 requests (Oroville Chamber of Commerce $15,000; The Oroville Initiative $10,000, cut from $20,750; Recreation Land/Vacationland/Info Book/ATV guide advertising $8,000; Oroville May Festival $5,000; Whistler Canyon trailhead vault toilet (Okanogan County Public Works) $5,000; Visitor Information Services $3,000; Oroville Market Association $2,900; Molson Museums $2,025). Council noted revenue is roughly $25,000 a year, so 2025 drew on fund balance and 'large approvals cannot be made every year.'
contact: JoAnn Denney, City Clerk, City of Oroville (phone/email not in retrieved documents; City Hall 1308 Ironwood St, Oroville, WA 98844); Mayor Ed Naillon
notes: Oroville takes written Hotel/Motel Tax applications each fall and the full City Council reviews them at its November budget workshop, then adopts the amounts in the budget; no separate LTAC is referenced (population under 5,000). Awards go to the chamber, May Festival, market association, museums, visitor information services, regional guide advertising and even a county trailhead toilet, so the program is open to a range of nonprofit and public applicants. Revenue is about $25,000 a year (DOR shows $34,402 in 2024) and the council has warned that 2025's $50,925 drew down reserves, so expect smaller awards. In Dec 2025 the council approved a chamber billing-insert flyer paid from the chamber's lodging tax award.

meeting_schedule: Council reviews hotel/motel applications at its November budget workshop (Nov 12, 2024) and acts at the following regular meeting (Nov 19, 2024); regular council meetings are the first and third Tuesdays
pool_note: 2025 approvals totaled $50,925 to eight outside applicants (the city kept nothing for its own projects), but annual revenue is only about $25,000, so the sustainable competitive pool is closer to $25,000; the $15,000 chamber grant is a recurring item that effectively reduces what is open to others to roughly $10,000-$35,000 depending on reserves.

name: South Bend
tax_rate: 4% local lodging tax under SBMC 3.20 (2% state-shared credit plus an additional 2% special tax); DOR flyer lists the special tax at 2% with a 10.2% total lodging rate; 2024 DOR distributions $7,188 (state-shared only)
contact: City of South Bend Administration (contacts page lists departments only; clerk name and phone not displayed), https://southbend-wa.gov/contacts/
notes: South Bend Municipal Code 3.20 levies the tax and directs proceeds to a special fund for tourism facilities, bonds and tourism advertising, but names no committee or application process, and the city website (southbend-wa.gov) has no lodging tax, tourism or forms page. Five searches of council records and Willapa Harbor Herald coverage returned nothing on how the roughly $7,000 a year is spent; the site links to the Willapa Harbor Chamber of Commerce, the likely recipient. Verify with City Hall; Pacific County is the realistic route for event funding.

name: Coulee Dam
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (total lodging tax rate 10%) per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions $14,471 ($7,236 state-shared + $7,236 special)
deadline_pattern: No application round: the town budgets a lump sum to the Grand Coulee Dam Area Chamber of Commerce each year and directs other requests to the chamber; the balance funds town parks and the visitor center
annual_pool: 2016 preliminary budget: $22,000 to the chamber; about $28,000 kept by the town for Douglas Park and Mason City Memorial Park upkeep (2015 reporting)
contact: Town of Coulee Dam Clerk-Treasurer (Stefanie Bowden in 2014 reporting; current staff not verified)
notes: Per The Star's coverage (2014-2015), Coulee Dam's council adopted a policy of handing most of its tourism marketing money to the Grand Coulee Dam Area Chamber of Commerce in a lump sum with the understanding that other groups (Ridge Riders Saddle Club, park district, Okanogan County Tourism) request funds from the chamber, while the town spends the rest on park maintenance, restrooms and visitor center staffing. No later policy change was found, and the town has no posted application, so outside applicants should approach the chamber. The town also sits partly in Grant and Douglas counties. Sources are a decade old; confidence is low.
meeting_schedule: Town Council sets allocations through the annual budget (hearings in November)
pool_note: No competitive pool: 2016 plan was $22,000 lump sum to the chamber (which redistributed roughly $9,000 to Ridge Riders, Okanogan County Tourism and the park district the prior year) and about $28,000 retained for town parks. Current-year figures not published.

funding_docs.title: The Star: Towns' tourism fund plans detailed (Nov 25, 2015)
funding_docs.summary: Coulee Dam gives its lodging tax to the chamber in a lump sum ($22,000 proposed for 2016), other requests go through the chamber; ~$28,000 used for park upkeep; also lists Grand Coulee and Electric City allocations.

funding_docs.title: The Star: Coulee Dam open to new tourism spending approach (Nov 19, 2014)
funding_docs.summary: Council endorsed Mayor Wilder's plan: $30,000 to the chamber for marketing, 25% reserve until fund reaches $50,000, town retains ~$39,000 for parks and visitor center; fund held ~$78,000.

name: Newport
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (total lodging tax rate 9.7%) per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions $16,297 ($8,148 state-shared + $8,148 special)
deadline_pattern: No fixed deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis and must be received at least two weeks before the event; funds must be used by December 31 with no carryover
annual_pool: Not published; awards capped at $1,000 per entity per calendar year, so the roughly $16,000 annual revenue supports a handful of small grants
contact: Nickole (City Clerk/Treasurer office), City of Newport, 509-447-6429, 200 S. Washington Ave, Newport, WA 99156 (mail applications Attn: City Clerk/Treasurer)
notes: Newport uses a one-page Hotel/Motel Tax Fund Application modeled on Washougal's: City Administration reviews requests (room nights, reliability, promotion of Newport beyond its borders, local spending) and recommends to the City Council, which decides. Awards are capped at $1,000 per entity per year and should not exceed 25% of the event's promotion budget unless the event is all-volunteer; broad tourism promotion and large overnight events are preferred. Reimbursement only, after hard-copy proof of advertising carrying the required city hotel/motel tax credit line. No LTAC is referenced on the form (cities under 5,000 population are not required to have one).

presentation.pattern: No presentation; written application reviewed by City Administration

meeting_schedule: No committee; council acts on administration recommendations at regular meetings
pool_note: Annual pool not published; DOR shows $16,297 in 2024 distributions and the per-entity cap is $1,000.

funding_docs.title: City of Newport Hotel/Motel Tax Fund Application
funding_docs.summary: Ongoing application, two-week lead time, $1,000 per entity per year cap, 25% of promotion budget limit, administration review criteria, reimbursement after proof of advertising, required credit line.

name: Stanwood
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (total lodging tax rate 11.3%) per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions withheld as confidential (too few lodging taxpayers to disclose)
notes: Stanwood created a Lodging Tax Advisory Committee by Ordinance 1513 in 2023 (SMC 2.14.050 gives it the standard 45-day review of proposals to impose, change or spend lodging tax), but four further searches of the city site, budget and Stanwood Camano News found no application, grant page, award record or committee roster, and DOR suppresses the city's revenue figure because it has too few lodging taxpayers. The committee exists to review the council's use of a very small fund, not to run a grant round. Verify with Stanwood City Hall; Snohomish County's Hotel-Motel Small Fund is the practical route for Stanwood-Camano events.

funding_docs.title: Stanwood Municipal Code 2.14.050 Recommendations on lodging tax funds
funding_docs.summary: LTAC review duties under Ord. 1513 (2023): proposals submitted at least 45 days before council action; comments on tourism impact and fund stability.

Call the City Clerk at 509-486-2132; Okanogan County's lodging tax program is the realistic route for events.

name: Ritzville
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax (total lodging tax rate 10%) per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions $60,169 ($30,084 state-shared + $30,084 special)
notes: No lodging tax application, LTAC page, council record or news coverage for the City of Ritzville was found in six searches of the city site, the Ritzville Adams County Journal and regional sources; results returned only DOR tables and unrelated cities. Ritzville's I-90 motels generate about $60,000 a year, among the largest sums in this batch, so an allocation process certainly exists but is not online. Ritzville's population (about 1,700) is under the 5,000 LTAC threshold, so expect council-budget allocations (chamber, Wheat Land Communities Fair, downtown events) rather than a published grant round. Contact Ritzville City Hall directly.

name: Index
tax_rate: 2% special hotel/motel tax under Index Municipal Code 3.32 (Ord. 511, 2024), applying to hotels, motels, trailer camps and short-term rentals; total lodging tax rate 11.1% per DOR Q1 2026 flyer; 2024 DOR distributions $13,526 (state-shared only)
notes: The Town of Index (population under 200) re-enacted its 2% lodging tax in 2024 (Ord. 511) with proceeds to a special fund for tourist promotion and tourism facilities under RCW 67.28; the code names no committee or application process and four searches of town records and regional sources found no grant round or award record. Revenue is about $13,500 a year and is most likely allocated in the town budget. Verify with Index Town Hall; Snohomish County's Hotel-Motel Small Fund is the practical route for Skykomish Valley events.
